Hi Lisa / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on requirements for the pilot:

Summary of requirements we captured:
- P95 latency target: 200ms (user-facing) for generation responses when using up to 2k input + 512 output tokens.
- Context window: support up to 4k total tokens for some edge flows; most traffic is ~2k.
- Streaming: partial token streaming required for the chat UI (low-latency first bytes is important).
- Throughput / concurrency: expected peak concurrent users ~200 (peak), steady-state 30-50 concurrent. Estimated peak requests/sec ~60.
- Quality: accuracy/formatting checks will be validated via our eval prompts; small allowed tail for extra-latency during long outputs.

Open questions for you (please confirm):
1) Are the 200ms P95 and streaming requirement mandatory for the pilot, or can we accept 300-350ms during initial integration?
2) For the 4k context window use cases, how often do you expect those to occur (percent of requests)?
3) Any restrictions on routing to hosted vs. private deployment for this pilot (data residency/SOC controls)?

What I propose as next steps:
- Dylan and Rafael to run a quick perf estimate based on the 2k/4k token profiles and provide a cost/architecture recommendation (hosted vs Dedicated) - ETA EOD tomorrow.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive (solutions engineering + infra) - propose Wed 5/13 10am PT.
- You (FinCo) to share any sample prompt/utterance distributions or a small synthetic dataset so we can simulate realistic token distributions.

Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- P95: 200ms is ideal for the primary chat flow (2k input / 512 output). We can tolerate up to 300ms for initial pilot during the first 30 days, but long term we want to be in the 200ms neighborhood.
- Context window: ~85% of requests are <=2k tokens, ~10% are 3-4k, and ~5% are >4k (those are rare batch/archival tasks and can be routed to non-streaming workers).
- Streaming: streaming partial outputs is required for the chat UI on desktop and mobile. First packet latency <100ms preferred, but not a hard block for pilot.
- Concurrency/throughput: the 200 concurrent number is peak for a campaign; typical is 30-40 concurrent. Peak QPS estimate of 60 is accurate.
- Data residency: pilot must run in our US region and logs must be retained for 90 days; we have SOC 2 and a separate security questionnaire in progress.

We'll upload a small sample of prompts and token distributions to the shared drive by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks Marissa / Lisa - quick technical notes and assumptions for the estimates: 

- Baseline assumption: target model is an open LLM comparable to a 13B dense model (we recommended a quantized variant for production).
- Latency impact by context window: token complexity grows roughly linearly for decoding with KV cache reads and attention overhead increases with longer contexts; expect ~1.7x-2.2x CPU/GPU time for 4k vs 2k depending on kernel optimizations.
- Streaming: partial token streaming will reduce perceived latency but requires connection-level multiplexing; first-byte delivery depends on model compilation and batch scheduling - we can hit <100ms first-byte with low-latency single-request execution, but throughput will constrain when batching is active.
- Concurrency/throughput: to meet P95 200ms for 2k token profiles at 60 RPS peak with 200 concurrent, recommendation is Dedicated reserved pool (multi-GPU) with concurrency sharding and a small hot-cache for common prefixes. Hosted can work for pilot if traffic is bursty and within quota, but tail latencies will be worse under load.

Action items for us: Rafael, can you produce a 3-line cost/infra estimate (hosted vs Dedicated) and a rough GPU-hours number for a two-week pilot? I'll draft the perf test harness and run a synthetic sim when we get the sample prompts.
